newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Supreme Court head reported ill in siege.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Supreme Court head reported ill in siege.

text.p: Peru's Supreme Court President Moises Pantoja, a hostage to Marxist guerrillas occupying the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, suffers a serious heart disease and needs urgent treatment, local newspapers said on Tuesday.

Hostages freed on Sunday night by the guerrillas reported that Pantoja was suffering from his heart condition and high blood pressure, the newspapers said. He was among more than 140 VIP hostages left inside the building.

The captives, who have now been there for seven nights, included President Alberto Fujimori's brother, Pedro Fujimori, along with top government officials, Japanese businessmen and a handful of ambassadors from Asia and Latin America.

Although Pantoja was believed to be in the worst condition, others were reportedly suffering diarrhoea and eye infections caused by unhygenic conditions inside the residence, which has been without running water for several days.
Pantoja's doctor, Rosa Busso, said he was due to go into hospital even before the crisis, according to the daily El Sol.
